name: withhuman
description: Human approval for AI agent tool calls, with human in the loop guardrails. Set rules for what runs automatically and what your team approves from Slack, Discord or your phone. Write and test them from ChatGPT or Codex.

interface.longDescription:
Human in the loop approvals for your AI agents. Let your agents work on their own, and have a person approve the actions that matter.

withHuman checks every tool call your agents make against your approval rules before it runs. Routine calls go straight through. The rest wait for someone on your team to approve or deny them.

You can write rules like:

"Let the support agent refund customers up to $20 automatically. Send larger refunds to the support team to approve first."

What you can do:

- Write and test rules. Preview a rule against sample requests, then turn it on.
- Ask the right people. Send requests to teams, with escalation levels and working hours.
- Use one set of rules for every agent. The same rules cover Claude Code, Codex, OpenClaw, Hermes and your own agents.
- Manage your agents and teams.
- See why a request was held.

You need a withHuman organization. Sign up at app.withhuman.ai, then connect your agents with the withhuman CLI. Your team approves requests in the web app, Slack, Discord, email or the withHuman phone app.
defaultPrompt: Show me the approval rules my agents follow
Send refunds over $20 to the support team to approve
Who gets notified when a request needs approval?

positive.description: Read the approval rules the organization's agents follow.
positive.prompt: Show me the approval rules my agents follow.
positive.expected_behavior: Reads the entry pipeline and explains its rules in plain words, including that the codex agent's git pushes go to the Engineering team for approval.

positive.description: Draft a new rule and preview it against sample requests without saving it.
positive.prompt: Send Stripe refunds over $20 from support-bot to the support team to approve. Show me what it would do before turning it on.
positive.expected_behavior: Proposes a rule on the support-bot agent, the refund tool and the refund amount. Previews a $50 refund (sent to the support path for a person) and a $10 refund (not held by the new rule). Asks before saving and saves nothing.

positive.description: Add a rule and turn it on after the user confirms.
positive.prompt: Make every git push from the codex agent wait for the engineering team, even on feature branches. Turn it on once I confirm.
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the change and a preview, waits for the user's confirmation, then saves a new entry pipeline revision and reports that it is active.

positive.description: Find out who is asked to approve requests.
positive.prompt: Who gets notified when a request needs approval?
positive.expected_behavior: Names each escalation path the rules use, its levels and timing, and the people on each team.

positive.description: Explain why a specific request was held for a person.
positive.prompt: Why was the last git push from the codex agent held for approval?
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the most recent held request from codex and explains which rule sent it to a person, which path was notified and how it was decided.

negative.description: Deciding requests is out of scope: people approve or deny requests in the withHuman app, Slack, Discord, email or the phone app, and the plugin has no tool for it. Expected: says it cannot approve requests and points to the app.
negative.prompt: Approve the pending refund request for me.

negative.description: Changing a person's role is out of scope: roles and invitations are managed only in the withHuman app. Expected: says it cannot change roles and points to Members in the withHuman app.
negative.prompt: Make jane@example.com an admin of our withHuman organization.

negative.description: Acting on another service is out of scope: withHuman sets approval rules for agents but does not issue refunds. Expected: does not call withHuman tools, and says withHuman cannot issue refunds itself.
negative.prompt: Refund $30 to the customer on Stripe charge ch_3PqX2.

publication.release_notes: First release. Write and preview approval rules for your AI agents, see who gets asked to approve, and find out why a request was held.
